821	            Drain frees room in the pack (the car returns from a trip lower
822	            than it left), so the routine top-up after a trip may buy the trip
823	            energy back — without this credit the allocator would treat the
824	            pack as still full and skip the recharge.
825	            """
826	            if battery_kwh <= 0:
827	                return float("inf")
828	            drained = sum(ev_request.drain_kwh.values())
829	            return max(
830	                0.0, ceiling_kwh - soc0_kwh + drained - sum(allocation.values())
831	            )
832	
833	        def select(
834	            deficit: float, candidates: list, room: float | None = None
835	        ) -> dict[datetime, float]:
836	            """Cost-optimal on/off full-power hours for ``deficit`` kWh.
837	
838	            ``candidates`` = eligible slots; hours partially taken by an
839	            earlier commitment keep their remaining headroom (topping them up
840	            is the same physical full-power hour). Returns headroom-filling on
841	            the cheapest hours plus the unavoidable remainder on the cheapest
842	            valid top-off hour. The car fills the chosen hours chronologically,
843	            so the remainder must sit on the chronologically last chosen hour.
844	            ``room`` overrides the pack-room cap (deadline targets compute the
845	            room *at their deadline*, which the global estimate can't see).
846	
847	            Placement preferences (``EVRequest.prefer_contiguous`` /
848	            ``prefer_early``) reshape the choice within a bounded extra cost:
849	            contiguity keeps the block unbroken unless the scattered optimum is
850	            more than ``contiguous_max_extra_pct`` % cheaper; earliness picks,
851	            among placements within ``early_max_extra_pct`` % of the cheapest,
852	            the one that finishes charging soonest.
853	            """
854	            deficit = min(deficit, capacity_left() if room is None else room)
855	            if deficit <= _EPS:
856	                return {}
857	            # Hours already carrying a partial allocation stay eligible with
858	            # their remaining headroom — an earlier small target (a trip floor)
859	            # must not fence the cheapest hour off from a later, bigger target
860	            # and scatter its block over pricier hours. Physically the charger
861	            # simply runs at full power through the union of the chosen hours.
862	            slots = sorted(
863	                (
864	                    s
865	                    for s in candidates
866	                    if charger_kw - allocation.get(s.start, 0.0) > _EPS
867	                ),
868	                key=lambda s: s.start,
869	            )
870	            if not slots:
871	                return {}
872	            caps = {
873	                s.start: charger_kw - allocation.get(s.start, 0.0) for s in slots
874	            }
875	            # Every variant must deliver the same energy or it isn't comparable
876	            # by cost (an under-filled variant would win on price alone).
877	            deliverable = min(deficit, sum(caps.values()))
878	
879	            hour_step = timedelta(hours=1)
880	
881	            def _contiguous(starts: list[datetime]) -> bool:
882	                # Consecutive clock hours; hours already charging from an
883	                # earlier commitment bridge gaps — the charger doesn't switch
884	                # off there, so the physical session is still unbroken.
885	                for a, b in zip(starts, starts[1:]):
886	                    h = a + hour_step
887	                    while h < b:
888	                        if allocation.get(h, 0.0) <= _EPS:
889	                            return False
890	                        h += hour_step
891	                return True
892	
893	            def _variant(
894	                top_off, fulls: list
895	            ) -> tuple[float, datetime, list[datetime], dict[datetime, float]]:
896	                covered = sum(caps[s.start] for s in fulls)
897	                rem = deliverable - covered  # in (0, cap(top_off)]
898	                cost = (
899	                    sum(caps[s.start] * slot_price(s) for s in fulls)
900	                    + rem * slot_price(top_off)
901	                )
902	                fill = {s.start: caps[s.start] for s in fulls}
903	                fill[top_off.start] = rem
904	                return (cost, top_off.start, [s.start for s in fulls], fill)
905	
906	            # One variant per candidate top-off hour: hours before it filled to
907	            # their headroom, cheapest first — forced ones until the top-off can
908	            # absorb the rest, then only hours cheaper than the top-off (each
909	            # displaces top-off energy), keeping a positive remainder on it.
910	            variants: list[
911	                tuple[float, datetime, list[datetime], dict[datetime, float]]
912	            ] = []
913	            for li, top_off in enumerate(slots):
914	                cap_top = caps[top_off.start]
915	                by_price = sorted(slots[:li], key=slot_price)
916	                fulls: list = []
917	                covered = 0.0
918	                i = 0
919	                while deliverable - covered > cap_top + _EPS and i < len(by_price):
920	                    fulls.append(by_price[i])
921	                    covered += caps[by_price[i].start]
922	                    i += 1
923	                if deliverable - covered > cap_top + _EPS:
924	                    continue  # this top-off can't hold the remainder
925	                p_top = slot_price(top_off)
926	                while i < len(by_price):
927	                    s = by_price[i]
928	                    i += 1
929	                    if slot_price(s) >= p_top:
930	                        break  # price-sorted → nothing cheaper follows
931	                    if deliverable - covered - caps[s.start] <= _EPS:
932	                        continue  # would leave no top-off remainder
933	                    fulls.append(s)
934	                    covered += caps[s.start]
935	                variants.append(_variant(top_off, fulls))
936	                # Contiguity candidate: the run of slots *immediately* before
937	                # the top-off, just long enough that the remainder fits on it
938	                # (valid when their clock hours chain up to the top-off).
939	                if fulls:
940	                    bfulls: list = []
941	                    bcov = 0.0
942	                    j = li - 1
943	                    while j >= 0 and deliverable - bcov > cap_top + _EPS:
944	                        bfulls.append(slots[j])
945	                        bcov += caps[slots[j].start]
946	                        j -= 1
947	                    block = list(reversed(bfulls))
948	                    if deliverable - bcov <= cap_top + _EPS and _contiguous(
949	                        [s.start for s in block] + [top_off.start]
950	                    ):
951	                        variants.append(_variant(top_off, block))
952	            if not variants:
953	                return {}
954	
955	            best_cost = min(v[0] for v in variants)
956	
957	            def _within(cost: float, pct: float) -> bool:
958	                # Bounded extra spend relative to the optimum; |·| keeps the
959	                # bound meaningful when spot prices go negative.
960	                return cost <= best_cost + abs(best_cost) * pct / 100.0 + _EPS
961	
962	            pool = variants
963	            if ev_request.prefer_contiguous:
964	                contiguous_pool = [
965	                    v
966	                    for v in variants
967	                    if _contiguous(sorted([*v[2], v[1]]))
968	                    and _within(v[0], ev_request.contiguous_max_extra_pct)
969	                ]
970	                # No block within budget → the gap is allowed (difference
971	                # exceeds the configured threshold).
972	                if contiguous_pool:
973	                    pool = contiguous_pool
974	            if ev_request.prefer_early:
975	                pool_best = min(v[0] for v in pool)
976	                budget = (
977	                    pool_best
978	                    + abs(pool_best) * ev_request.early_max_extra_pct / 100.0
979	                    + _EPS
980	                )
981	                eligible = [v for v in pool if v[0] <= budget]
982	                chosen = min(eligible, key=lambda v: (v[1], v[0]))
983	            else:
984	                chosen = min(pool, key=lambda v: v[0])
985	
986	            return dict(chosen[3])
987	
988	        def commit(chosen: dict[datetime, float]) -> None:
989	            for start, kwh in chosen.items():
990	                allocation[start] = allocation.get(start, 0.0) + kwh
991	
992	        # 1. Forced windows: full power in the user's chosen hours, chronological
993	        #    cap (the car can't take more than its room to the SoC ceiling).
994	        for start in sorted(ev_request.forced_hours):
995	            if start not in ev_request.available_hours or start not in slots_by_start:
996	                continue
997	            take = min(charger_kw, capacity_left())
998	            if take <= _EPS:
999	                break
1000	            allocation[start] = take
1001	
1002	        # 2. Deadline targets, earliest deadline first. Predicted trip drain
1003	        #    lowers what's in the pack, so the allocator buys that much more to
1004	        #    still hit the target — but only drain the car can charge *after*:
1005	        #    energy driven off past the last chargeable hour (the outbound leg
1006	        #    right before a trip deadline) cannot be bought back in time, and
1007	        #    crediting it overfilled the pack past its ceiling at departure.
1008	        #    Sizing a % deficit needs the live SoC; when the sensor is asleep
1009	        #    the targets are skipped rather than seeded from a fabricated 0 %
1010	        #    (which used to swing the plan by half a pack between cycles).
1011	        def drain_before(moment: datetime) -> float:
1012	            return sum(
1013	                kwh
1014	                for start, kwh in ev_request.drain_kwh.items()
1015	                if start < moment
1016	            )
1017	
1018	        targets = sorted(ev_request.targets, key=lambda t: t.deadline)
1019	        if targets and not soc_known and battery_kwh > 0:
1020	            _LOGGER.warning(
1021	                "EV: SoC niedostępny — cele procentowe pominięte w tym cyklu "
1022	                "(nie da się policzyć deficytu bez stanu naładowania)."
1023	            )
1024	            targets = []
1025	        for target in targets:
1026	            target_kwh = (
1027	                min(target.target_soc / 100.0 * battery_kwh, ceiling_kwh)
1028	                if battery_kwh
1029	                else 0.0
1030	            )
1031	            candidates = [
1032	                slot
1033	                for start, slot in slots_by_start.items()
1034	                if start < target.deadline and start in ev_request.available_hours
1035	            ]
1036	            last_charge_end = (
1037	                max(s.start for s in candidates) + timedelta(hours=1)
1038	                if candidates
1039	                else target.deadline
1040	            )
1041	            compensable = min(last_charge_end, target.deadline)
1042	            before = (
1043	                soc0_kwh
1044	                - drain_before(compensable)
1045	                + sum(
1046	                    kwh for start, kwh in allocation.items() if start < target.deadline
1047	                )
1048	            )
1049	            room_at_deadline = max(0.0, ceiling_kwh - before) if battery_kwh else None
1050	            commit(select(target_kwh - before, candidates, room=room_at_deadline))
1051	
1052	        # 3. Default top-up (no calendar plan).
1053	        if ev_request.required_kwh > _EPS:
1054	            candidates = [
1055	                slot
1056	                for start, slot in slots_by_start.items()
1057	                if start in ev_request.available_hours
1058	            ]
1059	            commit(select(ev_request.required_kwh, candidates))
1060

226	        ev_request: EVRequest | None = None,
227	        reminders: list[str] | None = None,

229	        battery = battery.copy()  # never mutate the live state
230	        slots = forecast.slots

240	        prices = [s.buy_price for s in slots if s.buy_price is not None]
241	        median_price = statistics.median(prices) if prices else 0.0
242	        energy_price = [

244	        ]

248	        demand = [max(0.0, s.total_consumption_kwh) for s in slots]

279	    def _efficiency_segments(self, ceff: float) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
280	        """Marginal charge-efficiency segments ``(width_kw, η)`` for the LP.
281	
282	        Built from the configured power→efficiency samples as the concave hull
283	        of ``stored(P) = P·η(P)``: each hull chord is one segment whose slope is
284	        the *marginal* efficiency over that power band. Slopes are non-increasing
285	        by construction, so a pure LP fills the best segment first and the fill
286	        order matches physics (charge power grows through the sweet spot before
287	        the tail where efficiency falls off). The rising low-power part of a real
288	        efficiency chart is convex and gets flattened by the hull — a deliberate
289	        approximation (slopes are clamped to ≤ 1 so the model can never store
290	        more than it draws), and the min-charge-power floor keeps the plan out
291	        of that region anyway. Without a curve: one flat-η segment.
292	        """
293	        cap = self.config.inverter_max_charge_kw
294	        curve = self.config.charge_efficiency_curve or []
295	        points = sorted(
296	            (float(p["kw"]), min(max(float(p["eff"]), 0.01), 1.0))
297	            for p in curve
298	            if float(p.get("kw", 0.0)) > _EPS
299	        )
300	        if not points or cap <= _EPS:
301	            return [(cap, ceff)]
302	
303	        stored_pts: list[tuple[float, float]] = [(0.0, 0.0)]
304	        prev_kw, prev_eff = 0.0, points[0][1]
305	        for kw, eff in points:
306	            if kw >= cap - _EPS:
307	                # Interpolate η at the inverter cap and stop — powers beyond
308	                # the cap are unreachable.
309	                if kw > cap + _EPS and kw > prev_kw:
310	                    frac = (cap - prev_kw) / (kw - prev_kw)
311	                    eff = prev_eff + (eff - prev_eff) * frac
312	                    kw = cap
313	                stored_pts.append((kw, kw * eff))
314	                break
315	            stored_pts.append((kw, kw * eff))
316	            prev_kw, prev_eff = kw, eff
317	        else:
318	            # Curve ends below the cap → extend flat with the last efficiency.
319	            stored_pts.append((cap, cap * points[-1][1]))
320	
321	        hull = _upper_hull(sorted(set(stored_pts)))
322	        segments: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
323	        for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(hull, hull[1:]):
324	            if x2 - x1 <= _EPS:
325	                continue
326	            segments.append((x2 - x1, min((y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1), 1.0)))
327	        return segments or [(cap, ceff)]

330	        self,
331	        battery: BatteryModel,

551	    def _build_plan(
552	        self,
553	        forecast: Forecast,
554	        battery: BatteryModel,
555	        charge: list[float],
556	        discharge: list[float],
557	        energy_price: list[float],
558	        distribution: list[float],
559	        total_price: list[float],
560	        demand: list[float],
561	        ev_kwh: list[float],
562	        charge_order_price: list[float] | None = None,
563	        ev_request: EVRequest | None = None,
564	        reminders: list[str] | None = None,
565	        stored: list[float] | None = None,
566	    ) -> Plan:
567	        cfg = self.config
568	        ceff = max(battery.charge_efficiency, _EPS)
569	        deff = max(battery.discharge_efficiency, _EPS)
570	        wear = battery.wear_cost
571	        n = len(total_price)
572	        charge_price = charge_order_price or [
573	            _charge_order_price(price) for price in total_price
574	        ]
575	        # EV SoC forecast: project the car's charge forward from its live SoC as
576	        # planned charging is delivered and predicted trip driving drains it.
577	        # Only possible when the SoC sensor and a battery size are known;
578	        # otherwise the line stays blank.
579	        ev_battery_kwh = ev_request.battery_kwh if ev_request else 0.0
580	        ev_drain = ev_request.drain_kwh if ev_request else {}
581	        # The projected EV SoC can never exceed the active charge ceiling — the
582	        # car's BMS stops there, so a line climbing past it would be fiction.
583	        ev_ceiling_kwh = (
584	            max(0.0, min(100.0, ev_request.charge_ceiling_soc)) / 100.0 * ev_battery_kwh
585	            if ev_request is not None and ev_request.charge_ceiling_soc is not None
586	            else ev_battery_kwh
587	        )
588	        ev_soc_kwh: float | None = (
589	            ev_request.current_soc / 100.0 * ev_battery_kwh
590	            if ev_request is not None
591	            and ev_request.current_soc is not None
592	            and ev_battery_kwh > 0
593	            else None
594	        )
595	        p_term = (
596	            cfg.terminal_price
597	            if cfg.terminal_price is not None
598	            else (sum(total_price) / n if n else 0.0)
599	        )
600	        # Economic thresholds implied by the objective (for the human-readable
601	        # trace; the actual decisions come from the global LP, which may deviate
602	        # because of SoC limits or because the energy is needed elsewhere).
603	        charge_threshold = ceff * (deff * p_term - wear)
604	        discharge_threshold = p_term + wear
605	
606	        decisions: list[Decision] = []
607	        for t, slot in enumerate(forecast.slots):
608	            c = charge[t] if charge[t] > _EPS else 0.0
609	            d = discharge[t] if discharge[t] > _EPS else 0.0
610	            ev = ev_kwh[t]
611	            tp = total_price[t]
612	
613	            soc_before = battery.soc
614	            cost_before = battery.energy_cost
615	
616	            stored_kwh = 0.0
617	            delivered = 0.0
618	            # Effective charge efficiency at the LP-chosen power (from the
619	            # efficiency-curve segments); flat η when no curve is configured.
620	            eff_t = (
621	                stored[t] / c
622	                if stored is not None and c > _EPS and stored[t] > _EPS
623	                else None
624	            )
625	            if c > 0:
626	                stored_kwh = battery.charge_from_grid(c, tp, efficiency=eff_t)
627	            if d > 0:
628	                delivered, _ = battery.discharge_to_load(d)
629	
630	            if stored_kwh > _EPS and stored_kwh >= delivered:
631	                mode = InverterMode.CHARGE
632	            elif delivered > _EPS:
633	                mode = InverterMode.DISCHARGE
634	            else:
635	                mode = InverterMode.PASSTHROUGH
636	
637	            grid_buy = max(0.0, demand[t] - delivered + c + ev)
638	
639	            decision = Decision(start=slot.start)
640	            decision.inverter_mode = mode
641	            decision.ev_charge = ev > 0
642	            decision.ev_charge_kwh = ev
643	            if ev_soc_kwh is not None:
644	                drain = ev_drain.get(slot.start, 0.0)
645	                ev_soc_kwh = min(ev_ceiling_kwh, max(0.0, ev_soc_kwh + ev - drain))
646	                decision.ev_soc = round(ev_soc_kwh / ev_battery_kwh * 100.0, 1)
647	            decision.charge_power = (
648	                ChargePower.LIMITED if ev > 0 else ChargePower.FULL
649	            )
650	            decision.battery_charge_kwh = stored_kwh
651	            # Grid-side charge power (kW) actually drawn this hour — what you set
652	            # on the inverter as "force charge X kW". Equals ``stored / η``
653	            # (reduced if the SoC ceiling clipped the charge mid-hour); the hour
654	            # slot is 1 h so kWh == average kW.
655	            decision.charge_power_kw = (
656	                stored_kwh / (eff_t or ceff) if stored_kwh > _EPS else 0.0
657	            )
658	            decision.battery_discharge_kwh = delivered
659	            decision.grid_buy_kwh = grid_buy
660	            decision.battery_soc = battery.soc
661	            decision.battery_energy_cost = battery.energy_cost
662	            decision.energy_cost = grid_buy * energy_price[t]
663	            decision.distribution_cost = grid_buy * distribution[t]
664	            decision.hour_cost = decision.energy_cost + decision.distribution_cost
665	            decision.fixed_cost = slot.distribution_fixed_hourly or 0.0
666	            decision.battery_use_cost = delivered * decision.battery_energy_cost
667	
668	            decision.trace = {
669	                "total_price": round(tp, 4),
670	                "total_price_raw": round(tp, 6),
671	                "charge_order_price": round(charge_price[t], 4),
672	                "energy_price": round(energy_price[t], 4),
673	                "distribution": round(distribution[t], 4),
674	                "terminal_price": round(p_term, 4),
675	                "charge_threshold": round(charge_threshold, 4),
676	                "discharge_threshold": round(discharge_threshold, 4),
677	                "demand_kwh": round(demand[t], 3),
678	                "ev_kwh": round(ev, 3),
679	                "charge_kwh": round(stored_kwh, 3),
680	                "charge_efficiency": round(eff_t, 4) if eff_t is not None else None,
681	                "discharge_kwh": round(delivered, 3),
682	                "grid_buy_kwh": round(grid_buy, 3),
683	                "soc_before": round(soc_before, 1),
684	                "soc_after": round(battery.soc, 1),
685	                "battery_energy_cost_before": round(cost_before, 4),
686	                "reason": self._reason(
687	                    mode, tp, charge_threshold, discharge_threshold, stored_kwh, delivered
688	                ),
689	            }
690	
691	            if t == 0 and reminders:
692	                decision.reminders = list(reminders)
693	
694	            decisions.append(decision)
695	
696	        return Plan(forecast=forecast, decisions=decisions, created_at=dt_util.now())

237	class EVRequest:
238	    """Structured EV charging need passed to the optimizer."""
239	
240	    enabled: bool = False
241	    required_kwh: float = 0.0
242	    charger_kw: float = 3.5
243	    phase: int = 1
244	    phases: int = 1
245	    battery_kwh: float = 60.0
246	    current_soc: float | None = None

251	    # Predicted energy out of the pack per hour (kWh) — trip driving. The

def _plan_ev(
        self, forecast: Forecast, ev_request: EVRequest | None
    ) -> dict[datetime, float]:
        """Allocate EV charging across the horizon.

        The charger is **on/off at full power** — it cannot dose a fraction of an
        hour. So reaching a deficit of ``D`` kWh means turning the charger on for
        ``K = ceil(D / P)`` hours (``P`` = full charge power); the car draws full
        power in each and its BMS tops off — leaving an unavoidable partial of
        ``D - (K-1)·P`` on whichever hour is **chronologically last** among the
        chosen ones (that is where charging actually finishes).

        Because that partial buys *less* energy, the cost-minimising choice is to
        spend full hours on the cheapest slots and let the partial land on a
        pricier slot — but only one that can legitimately be the top-off hour
        (i.e. has enough earlier hours to hold the full blocks). We therefore try
        every candidate top-off hour, pick the cheapest full blocks before it,
        and keep the globally cheapest combination. This is what stops the plan
        from e.g. wasting a whole expensive hour just to shave a few minutes.

        Three layers, never exceeding the request's SoC ceiling
        (``charge_ceiling_soc`` — the car is steered to stop there):

        1. **Forced windows** — bare ``"<keyword>"`` calendar events: charge full
           power in exactly those hours (user's explicit choice, not cost-driven).
        2. **Deadline targets** — ``"<keyword> NN%"`` events: cost-optimal blocks
           among available hours before the deadline (earliest deadline first).
        3. **Default top-up** — no calendar: cost-optimal blocks for the deficit
           to the target SoC.

        Predicted trip drain (``EVRequest.drain_kwh``) is folded in on both
        sides: deadline targets buy extra to cover driving the car can still
        recharge after (never the leg driven off after the last chargeable
        hour), and the room-to-ceiling cap credits energy the trips take back
        out of the pack.
        """
        if ev_request is None or not ev_request.is_actionable:
            return {}

        slots_by_start = {
            s.start: s for s in forecast.slots if s.buy_price is not None
        }

        def slot_price(slot) -> float:
            """Per-kWh price the EV actually pays in a slot.

            The charger is grid-fed, so it pays the FULL price — energy plus
            distribution — the same composition the battery LP optimises on.
            Ordering by ``buy_price`` alone picked hours that looked cheap on
            the energy component but were expensive once the TOU distribution
            band was added. Bucketed to the displayed grosz (like the battery
            charge order) so sub-grosz noise can't reshuffle equal-looking
            hours between planning cycles; sorts are stable, so grosz ties
            stay chronological.
            """
            return _charge_order_price(
                slot.buy_price + (slot.distribution_price_kwh or 0.0)
            )

        charger_kw = max(ev_request.charger_power_kw, 0.1)
        battery_kwh = max(ev_request.battery_kwh, 0.0)

        """Allocate EV charging across the horizon.

        The allocator sizes hours in **pack energy** ("added" kWh): a full
        charge hour adds ``P·η(P)`` at full power, so reaching a deficit of
        ``D`` kWh means ``K = ceil(D / (P·η))`` hours — full hours on the
        cheapest slots and the unavoidable remainder on whichever chosen hour
        is **chronologically last** (that is where charging actually
        finishes). We try every candidate top-off hour, pick the cheapest full
        blocks before it, and keep the globally cheapest combination (costs
        are grid-side: added energy ÷ the efficiency at the hour's power).

        The top-off hour depends on the current-control mode:

        * **full power** (legacy) — the car draws full power and its BMS stops
          mid-hour once the remainder is in;
        * **current control** — the hour runs at the smallest configured
          current whose full-hour yield covers the remainder, so a small
          top-up charges gently across the hour instead of a full-power
          burst; the chosen amps ship in the returned allocation.

        Three layers, never exceeding the request's SoC ceiling
        (``charge_ceiling_soc`` — the car is steered to stop there):

        1. **Forced windows** — bare ``"<keyword>"`` calendar events: charge full
           power in exactly those hours (user's explicit choice, not cost-driven).
        2. **Deadline targets** — ``"<keyword> NN%"`` events: cost-optimal blocks
           among available hours before the deadline (earliest deadline first).
        3. **Default top-up** — no calendar: cost-optimal blocks for the deficit
           to the target SoC.

        Predicted trip drain (``EVRequest.drain_kwh``) is folded in on both
        sides: deadline targets buy extra to cover driving the car can still
        recharge after (never the leg driven off after the last chargeable
        hour), and the room-to-ceiling cap credits energy the trips take back
        out of the pack.
        """

            return EVAllocation()

        slots_by_start = {
            s.start: s for s in forecast.slots if s.buy_price is not None
        }

        def slot_price(slot) -> float:
            """Per-kWh price the EV actually pays in a slot.

            The charger is grid-fed, so it pays the FULL price — energy plus
            distribution — the same composition the battery LP optimises on.
            Ordering by ``buy_price`` alone picked hours that looked cheap on
            the energy component but were expensive once the TOU distribution
            band was added. Bucketed to the displayed grosz (like the battery
            charge order) so sub-grosz noise can't reshuffle equal-looking
            hours between planning cycles; sorts are stable, so grosz ties
            stay chronological.
            """
            return _charge_order_price(
                slot.buy_price + (slot.distribution_price_kwh or 0.0)
            )

        # Power/efficiency model. The allocator sizes hours in pack ("added")
        # energy; grid energy = added ÷ η(P) at the hour's charging power.
        eff_curve = ev_request.efficiency_curve
        p_full = max(ev_request.charger_power_kw, 0.1)
        eff_full = _ev_efficiency_at(eff_curve, p_full)
        current_control = (
            ev_request.current_control
            and 1 <= ev_request.min_current_a <= ev_request.max_current_a

        def fit_for_added(added: float) -> tuple[float, int | None]:
            """(grid kWh, amps) to put ``added`` kWh into the pack in one hour.

            With current control: the smallest whole-amp level whose full-hour
            yield covers ``added`` (gentle top-off); the car's BMS still stops
            once the energy is in, so a need below the minimum level's yield
            simply ends mid-hour. Without: full power, mid-hour BMS stop.
            """

        battery_kwh = max(ev_request.battery_kwh, 0.0)

async def async_charging_efficiency(self, days: int = 30) -> dict:
        """Measured charging efficiencies from sensors, next to the configured ones.

        Informational only — the configured values stay authoritative for
        planning. EV: the grid-side charge-meter energy vs the car's
        energy-added counter, overall and bucketed by average charging power
        (so the measured points can be read against the configured efficiency
        curve). Battery: round-trip Σ discharge / Σ charge over the window vs
        the configured η_ch × η_dis (the SoC drift over a 30-day window is
        noise next to the cycled energy).
        """
        from .const import (
            CONF_BATTERY_CHARGE_SENSOR,
            CONF_BATTERY_DISCHARGE_SENSOR,
            CONF_CHARGE_EFFICIENCY,
            CONF_CHARGE_EFFICIENCY_CURVE,
            CONF_DISCHARGE_EFFICIENCY,
            CONF_EV_CHARGE_METER_SENSOR,
            CONF_EV_EFFICIENCY_CURVE,
            CONF_EV_ENERGY_ADDED_SENSOR,
            DEFAULTS,
        )
        from .optimizer import _ev_efficiency_at

        now = dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        start = now - timedelta(days=max(days, 1))
        _MIN_HOUR_KWH = 0.1  # ignore metering noise / idle hours

        async def _series(conf_key: str) -> tuple[str | None, dict]:
            eid = self.config.get(conf_key)
            if not eid:
                return None, {}
            return eid, await self.consumption.async_range_kwh(eid, start, now)

        def _r(value: float | None, nd: int = 3) -> float | None:
            return round(value, nd) if value is not None else None

        # ---- EV: charge meter (grid side) vs energy added (pack side) ----
        grid_eid, grid_series = await _series(CONF_EV_CHARGE_METER_SENSOR)
        added_eid, added_series = await _series(CONF_EV_ENERGY_ADDED_SENSOR)
        ev_curve = list(self.config.get(CONF_EV_EFFICIENCY_CURVE) or [])
        ev: dict = {
            "available": bool(grid_eid and added_eid),
            "grid_sensor": grid_eid,
            "added_sensor": added_eid,
            "hours": 0,
            "grid_kwh": None,
            "added_kwh": None,
            "measured_eff": None,
            "configured_curve": ev_curve,
            "buckets": [],
        }
        if grid_series and added_series:
            # Hourly kWh at 1-h slots == average kW → bucket by power (0.5 kW).
            buckets: dict[float, list[float]] = {}
            total_grid = total_added = 0.0
            hours = 0
            for hour, grid_kwh in grid_series.items():
                if grid_kwh < _MIN_HOUR_KWH:
                    continue
                added_kwh = added_series.get(hour, 0.0)
                hours += 1
                total_grid += grid_kwh
                total_added += added_kwh
                key = round(grid_kwh * 2) / 2.0
                agg = buckets.setdefault(key, [0.0, 0.0, 0])
                agg[0] += grid_kwh
                agg[1] += added_kwh
                agg[2] += 1
            ev.update(
                {
                    "hours": hours,
                    "grid_kwh": _r(total_grid),
                    "added_kwh": _r(total_added),
                    "measured_eff": (
                        _r(total_added / total_grid, 4) if total_grid > 0 else None
                    ),
                    "buckets": [
                        {
                            "power_kw": key,
                            "hours": int(n),
                            "grid_kwh": _r(g),
                            "added_kwh": _r(a),
                            "measured_eff": _r(a / g, 4) if g > 0 else None,
                            "configured_eff": (
                                _r(_ev_efficiency_at(ev_curve, key), 4)
                                if ev_curve
                                else None
                            ),
                        }
                        for key, (g, a, n) in sorted(buckets.items())
                    ],
                }
            )

        # ---- Battery: round-trip from the charge/discharge meters ----
        charge_eid, charge_series = await _series(CONF_BATTERY_CHARGE_SENSOR)
        dis_eid, dis_series = await _series(CONF_BATTERY_DISCHARGE_SENSOR)
        eta_c = float(self.config.get(CONF_CHARGE_EFFICIENCY, DEFAULTS[CONF_CHARGE_EFFICIENCY]))
        eta_d = float(self.config.get(CONF_DISCHARGE_EFFICIENCY, DEFAULTS[CONF_DISCHARGE_EFFICIENCY]))
        total_charge = sum(charge_series.values()) if charge_series else 0.0
        total_dis = sum(dis_series.values()) if dis_series else 0.0
        battery = {
            "available": bool(charge_eid and dis_eid),
            "charge_sensor": charge_eid,
            "discharge_sensor": dis_eid,
            "charge_kwh": _r(total_charge),
            "discharge_kwh": _r(total_dis),
            "measured_roundtrip": (
                _r(total_dis / total_charge, 4) if total_charge > 1.0 else None
            ),
            "configured_charge_eff": _r(eta_c, 4),
            "configured_discharge_eff": _r(eta_d, 4),
            "configured_roundtrip": _r(eta_c * eta_d, 4),
            "charge_curve_points": len(
                self.config.get(CONF_CHARGE_EFFICIENCY_CURVE) or []
            ),
        }

        return {
            "generated_at": dt_util.now().isoformat(),
            "window_days": days,
            "ev": ev,
            "battery": battery,
        }

@dataclass
class EVAllocation:
    """Per-hour EV charging schedule in both energy domains.

    ``added`` is what lands in the pack (drives the SoC forecast and compares
    against the car's energy-added sensor); ``grid`` is what flows through the
    meter (drives cost and the LP's grid load) — they differ by the charging
    efficiency at the hour's power. ``amps`` carries the planned charging
    current when current control is active (None per hour otherwise).
    """

    added: dict[datetime, float] = field(default_factory=dict)

"""EV charging-current control + efficiency curve in the allocator.

With ``current_control`` the top-off hour runs at the smallest configured
current whose full-hour yield covers the remainder (gentle top-ups instead of
a full-power burst), and the efficiency curve converts pack-side ("added")
energy into the grid-side draw the costs are paid on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import timedelta

from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util

from custom_components.powerpilot.models import Forecast, HourSlot
from custom_components.powerpilot.modules.ev import EVRequest
from custom_components.powerpilot.optimizer import (
    ChargeCurve,
    Optimizer,
    OptimizerConfig,
    _ev_efficiency_at,
)

H0 = dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(hours=1)

# 3 × 230 V charger: 5 A → 3.45 kW … 16 A → 11.04 kW.
CURVE = [
    {"kw": 3.45, "eff": 0.80},
    {"kw": 11.04, "eff": 0.90},
]


def _forecast(prices: list[float]) -> Forecast:
    return Forecast(
        slots=[
            HourSlot(
                start=H0 + timedelta(hours=i),
                buy_price=p,
                distribution_price_kwh=0.0,
                base_consumption_kwh=0.0,
            )
            for i, p in enumerate(prices)
        ]
    )


def _request(required_kwh: float, n_hours: int, **kwargs) -> EVRequest:
    return EVRequest(
        enabled=True,
        required_kwh=required_kwh,
        phases=3,
        battery_kwh=60.0,
        current_soc=0.0,
        available_hours={H0 + timedelta(hours=i) for i in range(n_hours)},
        current_control=True,
        min_current_a=5,
        max_current_a=16,
        voltage=230.0,
        **kwargs,
    )


def _optimizer() -> Optimizer:
    return Optimizer(
        OptimizerConfig(
            inverter_max_charge_kw=3.0,
            inverter_max_discharge_kw=3.0,
            charge_curve=ChargeCurve(default_kw=3.0),
        )
    )


def test_efficiency_interpolation() -> None:
    assert _ev_efficiency_at([], 5.0) == 1.0  # no curve → lossless (legacy)
    assert _ev_efficiency_at(CURVE, 1.0) == 0.80  # clamped below the range
    assert _ev_efficiency_at(CURVE, 20.0) == 0.90  # clamped above the range
    mid = _ev_efficiency_at(CURVE, (3.45 + 11.04) / 2)
    assert abs(mid - 0.85) < 1e-6  # linear between the samples


def test_small_top_up_fits_the_smallest_current() -> None:
    # 2 kWh into the pack: 5 A (3.45 kW) covers it in one gentle hour instead
    # of a full-power burst.
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(_forecast([0.10, 0.20]), _request(2.0, 2))
    assert list(alloc.added.values()) == [2.0]
    hour = next(iter(alloc.added))
    assert alloc.amps[hour] == 5
    assert alloc.grid[hour] == 2.0  # no curve on the request → lossless


def test_efficiency_curve_scales_the_grid_side() -> None:
    # 2 kWh added at the 5 A fit (3.45 kW → η 0.80) draws 2.5 kWh from the grid.
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(
        _forecast([0.10, 0.20]), _request(2.0, 2, efficiency_curve=CURVE)
    )
    hour = next(iter(alloc.added))
    assert alloc.amps[hour] == 5
    assert abs(alloc.added[hour] - 2.0) < 1e-6
    assert abs(alloc.grid[hour] - 2.0 / 0.80) < 1e-6


def test_full_hours_run_at_max_current() -> None:
    # A full-hour yield at 16 A / η 0.90 is 11.04 × 0.90 = 9.936 kWh added, so
    # 12 kWh needs a full cheapest hour plus a small top-off elsewhere.
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(
        _forecast([0.10, 0.30, 0.12]), _request(12.0, 3, efficiency_curve=CURVE)
    )
    full_yield = 11.04 * 0.90
    assert abs(sum(alloc.added.values()) - 12.0) < 1e-6
    fulls = [h for h, kwh in alloc.added.items() if abs(kwh - full_yield) < 1e-6]
    assert len(fulls) == 1
    assert alloc.amps[fulls[0]] == 16
    top_off = next(h for h in alloc.added if h not in fulls)
    # The ~2.06 kWh remainder fits the smallest current again.
    assert alloc.amps[top_off] == 5


def test_legacy_mode_keeps_full_power_and_no_amps() -> None:
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(
        _forecast([0.10, 0.20]),
        EVRequest(
            enabled=True,
            required_kwh=2.0,
            charger_kw=3.5,
            phases=1,
            battery_kwh=60.0,
            current_soc=0.0,
            available_hours={H0, H0 + timedelta(hours=1)},
        ),
    )
    assert list(alloc.added.values()) == [2.0]
    assert alloc.amps == {}
    assert alloc.grid == alloc.added

content.text:
Gotowe — wszystkie trzy punkty. **157 testów przechodzi**, frontend zbudowany, zmiany w drzewie roboczym (nie commitowane).

## 1. Skąd 28% zamiast 18% — to nie bug alokatora, tylko inna „rezerwa"

Cel przed wyjazdem liczy się jako **rezerwa EV + energia podróży**. Rezerwa nie pochodzi z ustawień integracji (`min_soc` 10% to minimum **baterii domowej**), tylko z osobnej, edytowalnej encji **`number.powerpilot_ev_minimalna_rezerwa_soc`, której domyślna wartość to 20%**. Stąd: 20% (rezerwa EV) + 8% (5,3 kWh podróży) = 28%, powrót na 20%. Jeśli chcesz rezerwę EV 10% — ustaw suwak tej encji na 10 (dashboard albo karta encji). Żeby to było widoczne na przyszłość, karta EV w Statusie pokazuje teraz rozbicie przy każdym celu wyjazdowym: „min 28% = rezerwa EV 20% (encja …) + podróż 8%".

## 2. Dobór prądu ładowania + krzywa sprawności

W ustawieniach EV doszły pola: **„Dobieraj prąd ładowania"** (wył. = powrót do „zawsze pełna moc"), **min/maks prąd (A)** (domyślnie 5–16) i **krzywa sprawności EV** — ten sam format tekstowy co krzywa baterii, np. z Twojego wykresu:
`1150:77.4, 1400:82.5, 1800:83.8, 2300:83.8, 3000:86.1, 3450:86.3, 3700:87.3, 4100:87.4, 5500:90.8, 6900:92.7, 9000:91, 11000:91`

Działanie (nowa wersja alokatora `amp-fit-efficiency-2026-07`):
- pełne godziny ładowania idą na **maksymalnym prądzie** (wg krzywej i tak najsprawniejszym), a **godzina dopełniająca** dostaje najmniejszy prąd, którego pełna godzina pokrywa resztę — doładowanie 10% nie odpala już pełnej mocy;
- krzywa sprawności rozdziela energię **z sieci** (koszty, obciążenie przyłącza, LP) od energii **dodanej do auta** (prognoza SoC, porównanie z sensorem „energy added") — plan `ev_charge_kwh` to teraz strona auta, nowe pole `ev_grid_kwh` to strona sieci;
- nowy sensor **`sensor.powerpilot_ev_prad_ladowania`** (A) podaje prąd dla aktywnej/najbliższej godziny ładowania — do automatyzacji sterującej ładowarką; wartość jest też w karcie EV („Sterowanie"). Domyślnie opcja jest **wyłączona** (zachowanie jak dotąd) — włącz ją w ustawieniach EV.

## 3. Zakładka „Sprawność"

Nowa zakładka (między Przepływem a Statusem) liczy sprawności **z istniejących sensorów** za 30 dni i zestawia z ustawieniami — z wyraźną notką, że **ustawienia są nadrzędne, pomiar informacyjny**:
- **EV**: licznik ładowarki (sieć) vs „energia dodana" (auto) — łącznie i w kubełkach po średniej mocy godziny, obok wartość z wpisanej krzywej dla tej mocy + różnica w p.p. To pokazuje wprost, czy tabelka z wykresu jest aktualna dla Twojej instalacji;
- **Bateria domowa**: round-trip Σrozładowanie/Σładowanie vs η_ład × η_rozład z ustawień.

Nie trzeba było nowych sensorów w konfiguracji — używa już wskazanych (licznik ładowarki EV, energy added, ładowanie/rozładowanie baterii); gdy któregoś brakuje, karta mówi który wskazać.

# Bumped whenever the EV allocation strategy changes. Surfaced in the debug dump
# so it's obvious from a JSON paste whether the running code is the current
# allocator or a stale import.
EV_ALLOCATOR_VERSION = "amp-fit-efficiency-2026-07"


def _ev_efficiency_at(curve: list[dict], power_kw: float) -> float:
    """AC charging efficiency at a total charging power (linear interpolation).

    ``curve`` holds {"kw","eff"} samples from a measured chart; outside the
    sampled range the nearest end value applies. No curve → lossless (1.0),
    the legacy behaviour.
    """
    points = sorted(
        (float(p["kw"]), min(max(float(p["eff"]), 0.01), 1.0))
        for p in (curve or [])
        if float(p.get("kw", 0.0)) > _EPS
    )
    if not points:
        return 1.0
    if power_kw <= points[0][0]:
        return points[0][1]
    if power_kw >= points[-1][0]:
        return points[-1][1]
    for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(points, points[1:]):
        if x1 <= power_kw <= x2:
            if x2 - x1 <= _EPS:
                return y2
            return y1 + (y2 - y1) * (power_kw - x1) / (x2 - x1)
    return points[-1][1]

class EVAllocation:
    """Per-hour EV charging schedule in both energy domains.

    ``added`` is what lands in the pack (drives the SoC forecast and compares
    against the car's energy-added sensor); ``grid`` is what flows through the
    meter (drives cost and the LP's grid load) — they differ by the charging
    efficiency at the hour's power. ``amps`` carries the planned charging
    current when current control is active (None per hour otherwise).

    The mapping interface exposes the primary (pack-side) schedule — an
    ``EVAllocation`` reads like the ``{hour: added kWh}`` dict it replaced.
    """

    added: dict[datetime, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    grid: dict[datetime, float] = field(default_factory=dict)

content.text: Backend czysty. Przepisuję testy na minuty + płaską sprawność:

input.content:
"""EV charging minutes + flat charging efficiency in the allocator.

The charger always runs at full power; each planned hour carries how many
minutes within it the charger should run (the user's automation stops it),
and the flat efficiency converts pack-side ("added") energy into the metered
grid draw the costs are paid on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import timedelta

from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util

from custom_components.powerpilot.models import Forecast, HourSlot
from custom_components.powerpilot.modules.ev import EVRequest
from custom_components.powerpilot.optimizer import (
    ChargeCurve,
    Optimizer,
    OptimizerConfig,
)

H0 = dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(hours=1)

# 3 × 3.68 kW = 11.04 kW full charger power, 91 % efficient at full power.
CHARGER_KW = 3.68
PHASES = 3
EFF = 0.91
P_FULL = CHARGER_KW * PHASES
HOUR_YIELD = P_FULL * EFF  # ≈ 10.05 kWh added per full hour


def _forecast(prices: list[float]) -> Forecast:
    return Forecast(
        slots=[
            HourSlot(
                start=H0 + timedelta(hours=i),
                buy_price=p,
                distribution_price_kwh=0.0,
                base_consumption_kwh=0.0,
            )
            for i, p in enumerate(prices)
        ]
    )


def _request(required_kwh: float, n_hours: int, **kwargs) -> EVRequest:
    return EVRequest(
        enabled=True,
        required_kwh=required_kwh,
        charger_kw=CHARGER_KW,
        phases=PHASES,
        battery_kwh=60.0,
        current_soc=0.0,
        available_hours={H0 + timedelta(hours=i) for i in range(n_hours)},
        charge_efficiency=EFF,
        **kwargs,
    )


def _optimizer() -> Optimizer:
    return Optimizer(
        OptimizerConfig(
            inverter_max_charge_kw=3.0,
            inverter_max_discharge_kw=3.0,
            charge_curve=ChargeCurve(default_kw=3.0),
        )
    )


def test_flat_efficiency_scales_the_grid_side() -> None:
    # 2 kWh into the pack draws 2 / 0.91 ≈ 2.198 kWh from the grid.
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(_forecast([0.10, 0.20]), _request(2.0, 2))
    hour = next(iter(alloc.added))
    assert abs(alloc.added[hour] - 2.0) < 1e-6
    assert abs(alloc.grid[hour] - 2.0 / EFF) < 1e-6


def test_small_top_up_gets_short_minutes() -> None:
    # 2 kWh added at a ~10.05 kWh/h full-power yield ≈ 12 minutes of charging.
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(_forecast([0.10, 0.20]), _request(2.0, 2))
    hour = next(iter(alloc.added))
    assert alloc.minutes[hour] == 12


def test_full_hours_get_60_minutes_and_top_off_the_rest() -> None:
    # 12 kWh needs one full cheapest hour (60 min) plus a ~2 kWh top-off.
    alloc = _optimizer()._plan_ev(_forecast([0.10, 0.30, 0.12]), _request(12.0, 3))
    assert abs(sum(alloc.added.values()) - 12.0) < 1e-6
    fulls = [h for h, kwh in alloc.added.items() if abs(kwh - HOUR_YIELD) < 1e-6]
    assert len(fulls) == 1

Oba punkty gotowe — **157 testów przechodzi**, frontend zbudowany. Do tego zostało w drzewie wcześniejsze podwyższenie wykresu cen (+40%), więc wszystko pójdzie razem.

## 1. Uproszczone ładowanie EV: pełna moc + jedna sprawność + minuty

Wycofałem dobór prądu (5–16 A) i krzywą sprawności — całość zastąpiona prostszym modelem:
- **Ustawienia EV**: jedno pole „Sprawność ładowania EV przy pełnej mocy" (suwak 0.50–1.00) — wpisujesz **0.91**. Pola prądu i krzywej zniknęły; ładowarka zawsze planowana na pełną moc (`moc na fazę × fazy`, jak pierwotnie).
- **Minuty ładowania w godzinie**: każda planowana godzina niesie czas pracy ładowarki — pełne godziny 60 min, godzina dopełniająca `ceil(potrzeba / (moc·η) × 60)`, np. doładowanie 2 kWh przy 11 kW → **12 min** (zaokrąglane w górę, żeby auto nie dostało mniej niż plan).
- **Ekspozycja**: nowy sensor **`EV minuty ładowania w godzinie`** (dla aktywnej godziny ładowania, a poza nią — dla najbliższej zaplanowanej; start masz w istniejącym `EV początek ładowania` — Twoja automatyzacja startuje ładowarkę o starcie i wyłącza po X minutach). Minuty widać też: w tooltipie wykresu energii („EV: 12 min ładowania" w nagłówku godziny — także dla godzin minionych i przypiętych prognoz, ze snapshotów), w karcie EV w Statusie („Minuty w godzinie") i w kaflu „EV: ładuje (12 min)" na Przeglądzie.
- Sprawność 0.91 rozdziela energię z sieci (koszty, LP) od dodanej do auta (SoC, porównanie z sensorem) — zakładka Sprawność porównuje teraz pomiar z tą jedną wartością.
- Wersja alokatora: `minutes-flat-eff-2026-07`.

## 2. Tryb falownika bieżącej godziny — naprawiony

Przyczyna: dla godziny w toku wykres wyznaczał tryb ze **zmierzonych przepływów** (statystyki 5-minutowe). 7 minut po pełnej godzinie rozładowanie miało < 0,05 kWh (próg szumu) → „passthrough", mimo że falownik faktycznie rozładowywał. Teraz bieżąca godzina pokazuje tryb z **zatwierdzonej decyzji planu** — dokładnie to, co raportuje sensor `Tryb falownika` (godziny zakończone dalej pokazują tryb zmierzony). Dodany test regresyjny.

    started yet) then surfaced as a phantom "21 → 28 %" jump on the next
    hour's tooltip although that hour had no charging planned at all.

    assert plan is not None and plan.decisions
    plan.decisions[0].battery_soc = 77.7  # planned end of the current hour

Oba zgłoszenia to były realne bugi — naprawione, **158 testów przechodzi**.

## Skąd uparte „min 28%" mimo rezerwy 10%

Znalazłem właściwą przyczynę (moja wcześniejsza odpowiedź „ustaw encję na 10%" była niepełna): w `async_setup_entry` **pierwszy plan liczy się PRZED dodaniem encji number** (`first_refresh` przed `forward_entry_setups`). W tym momencie `min_soc_entity` jeszcze nie istnieje, więc moduł EV bierze wbudowany domyślny **20%** (a cel ładowania 80%), ignorując Twoje zapisane 10%. A że **każda zmiana ustawień robi reload integracji**, to po każdej zmianie (a robiłeś ich dziś sporo — plan z 16:29 to właśnie po-reloadowy) dostawałeś świeży plan z rezerwą 20% → cel podróży 20+8 = 28%. Poprawka działała dopiero od kolejnej pełnej godziny.

Fix: obie encje number po podpięciu (`async_added_to_hass`) **wymuszają przeliczenie planu** — kilka sekund po starcie/reloadzie plan liczy się już z odtworzonymi wartościami. Dodatkowo **zmiana suwaka też od razu przelicza plan** (wcześniej czekała do pełnej godziny — kolejny powód, czemu „nic się nie działo" po ustawieniu 10%). Po tej poprawce cel dla treningu pokaże „min 18% = rezerwa 10% + podróż 8%".

## Skok SoC EV 21→28% o 17:00 bez ładowania

To był błąd łańcucha prognozy w serii wykresu. Plan z 16:29 zaplanował doładowanie EV **w bieżącej godzinie (16:xx)** — jego koniec godziny to 28%. Ale prognozowe wiersze przyszłych godzin startowały od **żywego odczytu SoC** (21%, bo ładowanie fizycznie nie ruszyło), a kończyły na wartościach z planu — cała różnica objawiała się jako widmowy skok „21 → 28 ↑7" w tooltipie 17:00, choć ta godzina nic nie ładowała. Teraz pierwsza przyszła godzina startuje od **planowanego stanu końca bieżącej godziny** (`SoC` i `SoC EV` z decyzji), więc skok pokaże się tam, gdzie plan faktycznie ładuje (w wierszu bieżącej godziny, w kolumnie „prognoza"), a kolejne godziny są ciągłe. Dodany test regresyjny.

Zmiany w drzewie roboczym (razem z niczym więcej — poprzednia partia poszła w `c15e43b`). Mogę zrobić commit + push (`fix(ev): first plan after reload ignored restored SoC numbers; seed future SoC chain from current decision`) — potwierdź, albo najpierw sprawdź w HA: po restarcie „min" przy wyjeździe powinno w ciągu paru sekund zejść do 18%, a tooltip 17:00 przestać pokazywać skok.
